source_identity.source_control_rule: Approved rapid development requires authoritative source_commit and source_tree readback from the imported root; approval fields cannot create source identity.

purpose: Authorize a source-preserving project adoption, copy, normalization, or reconstruction without mutating the source before cutover.

preservation_root_refs.rule: Persist only opaque references; resolve host paths only at the execution boundary.

source_preservation.rule: Preserve exact included bytes before migration; exclude and record secrets, generated material, temporary material, and unsafe objects; never mutate the source before cutover.

rapid_development.rule: Imported projects remain discovery-only until the owner explicitly approves rapid development.

controller_planning.rule: The Controller derives the project-applicable roster and roadmap. Bootstrap and the Agent Spawner must not embed a fixed project roster.
controller_planning.automatic_continuation: Routine passed gates start the next eligible transition before the Controller turn ends; owner review is protected-boundary-only.

universal_closeout.rule: Imported-project temporary tasks use the general closeout contract in every import mode. Rapid development remains discovery-only until explicit owner approval; after approval, the Controller preserves and integrates each handoff, closes stale worktrees, removes active task scope, marks the chat out of scope, and dynamically archives the visible task.

storage_rule: External control-plane storage keeps preservation artifacts outside the product root by default. Project-sidecar storage is allowed only when the owner explicitly opts into an in-project control plane.
cutover_rule: A full normalize or reconstruct mode requires Controller-derived specialist coverage, Platform and Central integration, independent re-audit, exact candidate identity, and reversible cutover. Product source files remain unchanged before cutover; preservation artifacts are written only to the bound control-plane storage root.
